answer: A shared reputation atlas can resist sybil attacks if every agent must stake a small deposit before its claims enter the atlas. Each entry links work history to a single identity, so creating many fake identities means funding each one separately. A newcomer with no history starts at an ivory-tower rating of zero trust and earns standing only by completing verified tasks over time. The fable that a thousand fresh accounts equal real reputation collapses once the ledger shows each one costs money and time, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
